name: Acute Cholecystitis, Critical View of Safety and Biliary Injury

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Tokyo Guidelines 2018
clinicalPearls: Acute cholecystitis: cystic duct gallstone impaction; ultrasound shows wall thickening >4 mm, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy sign
Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours of symptom onset reduces complications and hospital stay compared to delayed repair
Strasberg Critical View of Safety requires 3 criteria: hepatocystic triangle cleared of fat, lower third of gallbladder mobilized off cystic plate, only 2 structures seen entering gallbladder
Strasberg bile duct injuries: Type A minor cystic leak, Type D lateral duct laceration, Type E complete transection of main common bile duct
Charcot triad (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain) and Reynolds pentad (+ shock, altered mental status) define acute cholangitis, requiring emergency ERCP decompression
reference.pathophysiology: Persistent cystic duct obstruction leads to mucosal ischemia, secondary bacterial invasion and transmural gallbladder inflammation. Failure to achieve the critical view of safety during laparoscopic cholecystectomy leads to misidentification of the common bile duct as the cystic duct, causing catastrophic duct transection or clipping.
additionalDifferentials: Acute acalculous cholecystitis in critically ill patients
additionalInvestigations: Right upper quadrant transabdominal ultrasound as first-line imaging
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) for choledocholithiasis or duct injury
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for therapeutic stone extraction or stenting
